$comment: HAND-EDITED source of the Developer Tools row: Inspect Element and the Web Inspector or Chromium DevTools for cmux's own pages. gen-settings-sources.py writes the Swift descriptor and parser constants. Row fields: see schemas/settings/source/updates.json.

lists.name: developerTools
lists.note: Settings > Advanced > Developer Tools (Lawrence 2026-11-07: "make it possible to open chrome devtools in chat ui itself").

rows.note: On (the default, in every build): the agent chat, Home, Markdown and Settings pages offer Inspect Element in their right-click menu, and Toggle Developer Tools (Cmd-Opt-I), Inspect Element (Cmd-Opt-C) and the palette's Developer Tools commands act on them. Off: only browser tabs open developer tools. Browser tabs are never affected.

help.text: Inspect Element and ⌥⌘I in chats, Home, Markdown and Settings.

lists.name: internalDeveloperMode
lists.note: Settings > Development (DEV and NIGHTLY only) > Internal Developer Mode (Lawrence 2026-11-09: "move all debug things to cmd shift p that is only visible when cmux internal developer mode is toggled on").

rows.note: Off (the default): the Command Palette lists no debug commands. On: every debug-only action is a palette row titled "Debug: <name>" (playgrounds, Debug Settings, the latency HUD); there is no Debug menu. DEV and NIGHTLY only: Release and RC builds have no debug actions and never show this row. Scripts (the CLI, MCP) run debug actions in DEV and NIGHTLY whatever this is.

help.text: Shows "Debug: …" commands in the Command Palette.

lists.name: relaunchCover
lists.note: Settings > Development (DEV and NIGHTLY only) > App Relaunch: how a relaunch swaps each window's saved picture for its live content, for comparing the swaps.

rows.note: How an app relaunch (an update, or `cmux app quit --keep-sessions`) swaps each window's saved picture (the relaunch cover) for its live content. off (the default): no picture is shown (the behavior before relaunch covers). instant: each window's picture is removed in one frame once all its panes are ready. crossfade: the window's picture fades out over 120 ms at that moment. progressive: each pane's region of the picture fades out over 80 ms as that pane becomes ready. A comparison setting for judging the swap: a row in Settings > Development and the Command Palette in DEV and NIGHTLY; the CLI and MCP set it in every build.

help.text: How a relaunched window swaps its saved picture for live content.

choices.note: No picture: windows open with their live content as it loads.
The window's picture goes in one frame once all its panes are ready.
The window's picture fades out over 120 ms once all its panes are ready.
Each pane's region of the picture fades out over 80 ms as that pane becomes ready.
